test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the main reason for the high population growth in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**High birth rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary reason for the high population growth in India is the **natural increase**, which is the difference between the **birth rate** and the **death rate**. While India has successfully brought down the death rate, the birth rate has remained relatively high for a long period. ***Hence, the option High birth rate is correct.***
 
• **High birth rate** refers to the number of live births per **1,000 persons** in a year. Factors such as **universal marriage**, **early marriage**, and **poverty** contribute to this high rate.
 
• **Low literacy rate** is a significant socio-economic factor that contributes to a high birth rate because of a lack of awareness regarding **family planning** and **contraception**. However, it is a cause of the birth rate rather than the direct statistical reason for population volume increase. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• A **high death rate** would actually result in a decrease or stagnation of the population. India has significantly reduced its death rate from **25 per 1,000** in **1951** to around **7.3 per 1,000** in recent years due to better **healthcare** and **nutrition**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• **High migration** refers to the movement of people into a country. While **international migration** affects population, the growth in India is predominantly driven by **natural increase** (births minus deaths) rather than people moving into the country from abroad. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Demographic Transition**: India is currently in the **third stage** of the **Demographic Transition Model**. This stage is characterized by a rapidly declining **death rate** and a slowly declining **birth rate**, leading to a high total population.
 
• **Total Fertility Rate (TFR)**: According to the **National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5)** conducted between **2019-21**, India’s **TFR** has declined to **2.0**, which is below the **replacement level** of **2.1**. This suggests that the population will eventually stabilize, though it continues to grow currently due to **population momentum**.
 
• **Global Standing**: In **April 2023**, the **United Nations** reported that **India** surpassed **China** to become the **world’s most populous country**, with a population exceeding **1.42 billion**.
 
• **Impact of Poverty**: In many Indian households, children are viewed as **economic assets** or additional **earning members**. This perspective, prevalent in the **unorganized sector** and **rural agriculture**, encourages larger family sizes.
 
• **Life Expectancy**: Due to advancements in **medical science** and **public health**, the average **life expectancy** in India has increased from approximately **32 years** in **1947** to over **70 years** in **2023**, contributing to the overall population count.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Population Policy (NPP) 2000**: The **Government of India** introduced this policy with the immediate objective of addressing unmet needs for **contraception** and **healthcare infrastructure**. The long-term goal is to achieve a **stable population** by **2045**.
 
• **Family Planning Programme**: India was the **first country in the world** to launch a **National Programme for Family Planning** in **1952**. It aimed to reduce birth rates to stabilize the population at a level consistent with the **national economy**.
 
• **Census Data**: The **2011 Census** of India showed a **decadal growth rate** of **17.7%**. The census is conducted every **10 years** by the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner** under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**.
 
• **Age Structure**: India possesses a **demographic dividend**, meaning a large percentage of its population is in the **working-age group** (**15-64 years**). This **youth bulge** ensures that even with lower fertility rates, the population will continue to grow for a few decades because of the sheer number of people in the **reproductive age** bracket.
